app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

final_report.root_cause: The Java-based ad container in pod ad-cb8574cd-rfpns was OOM-killed (Exit Code 137) because its memory limit was set to 300Mi, which is insufficient for the JVM during startup. The OOM kills prevented the pod from becoming Ready, caused CrashLoopBackOff/backoff events, and made the 'ad' service intermittently unavailable. This unavailability produced blocking/retries in the frontend call path and high tail latency observed at frontend-proxy.
affected_resources: request traces referencing traceID=80441c9f61c0d7aa27357b402ba0b0ff (shows frontend-proxy->frontend roundtrips ending at ad)
final_report.evidence_summary: kubectl describe and container status show Last State=Terminated, Exit Code=137 (SIGKILL) and Restart Count > 0; events show BackOff and repeated readiness probe failures (connection refused). Pod spec sets memory request and limit to 300Mi. Container logs only contain JVM startup warnings with no application stacktrace or graceful exit messages, consistent with abrupt kill. A sampled trace (traceID=80441c9f61c0d7aa27357b402ba0b0ff) shows high latency (≈2834 ms) with repeated frontend-proxy <-> frontend round-trips that terminate at 'ad', correlating ad unavailability with elevated latency upstream. Service 'ad' exists and has an endpoint, ruling out a missing Service/name mismatch.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority #1 investigation (completed): examined pod ad-cb8574cd-rfpns via kubectl describe and logs; diagnosed Exit Code 137 OOM kills during JVM startup with readiness probe failures causing CrashLoopBackOff. Priority #2 investigation (completed): validated frontend calls the 'ad' service and that the Kubernetes Service exists with a healthy-looking endpoint (10.244.1.32:8080), eliminating service-name/port misconfiguration. Together these show the root operational failure is the ad pod being OOMKilled rather than network/service misconfiguration or an application startup exception. No further tasks are required to localize the root cause; optional follow-ups (not required to conclude) would be to review pod memory metrics and JVM heap settings to size limits appropriately and to inspect other ad pods (if any) and dependency health.
